routes.description: Establish God through convergent natural-theology inferences from dependent causation, moral obligation, and the intelligibility of personal knowledge.
routes.successCriteria: The observed features must warrant a necessary divine source, objective moral ground, or personal knower sufficiently connected to the God asserted by the motion.

motionBridge.description: The convergent inferences must warrant identifying their ultimate explanatory ground as God.

centralBridges.description: Dependent change and causal actualization must terminate in a necessary, purely actual source.
Objective moral obligations must require a divine intellect beyond human opinion.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Natural-theology inference must remain a legitimate route from observed effects to an extranatural explanation.
Interpersonal knowledge must be capable of warranting belief beyond scientific testing alone.

routes.description: Withhold belief unless the affirmative defines and evidentially connects its proposed explanations to God while addressing naturalistic alternatives and hiddenness.
routes.successCriteria: The affirmative burden remains unmet if causal, moral, methodological, or personal-experience premises do not demonstrate the asserted divine conclusion.

motionBridge.description: Belief in God need not be accepted unless the affirmative supplies a defined and supported demonstration.

centralBridges.description: A first explanatory cause must not be identified with a divine mind without further support.
Objective moral assessment must be explainable relative to well-being without requiring divine moral law.
A capable God who wants belief must be reconciled with absent or unverifiable disclosure.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explanatory candidates must be demonstrable before they enter evidence-based inference.
The skeptical conclusion must remain revisable upon a valid argument supported by evidence.

sections.title: Burden of proof and warranted belief
sections.rationale: The governing evidential threshold determines what the affirmative must establish and when skeptical nonacceptance remains warranted.

sections.title: Causal dependence and identification of God
sections.rationale: The principal Thomistic route requires both a terminus for dependent actualization and a warranted identification of that terminus with God.

sections.title: Natural theology and scientific inference
sections.rationale: The legitimacy of inferring an extranatural explanation from natural observations controls whether the proposed proofs qualify as evidence for the motion.

sections.title: Objective morality and divine grounding
sections.rationale: The moral-law route turns on whether objective moral assessment requires a divine intellect or can arise from a stipulated secular foundation.

sections.title: Divine hiddenness and personal knowledge
sections.rationale: The clash concerns whether unverifiable disclosure counts against a belief-seeking God and whether interpersonal knowledge can warrant belief without scientific proof.
